title: Understanding Cat Behavior: Signals Your Feline Uses Daily
author: Thompson P.
summary: Decode tail flicks, slow blinks, and the subtle ways cats communicate comfort, stress, and curiosity at home.
content: Cats rely on body language long before they meow. A slow blink shows trust, while an upright tail signals a friendly greeting. Flattened ears or a twitching tail can warn that a cat needs space.
To build a calmer home, keep routines predictable and provide vertical spaces. Offer scratching posts in busy areas so the cat can mark territory without damaging furniture.
If you spot over-grooming or hiding, treat it as a stress signal. Add more hiding spots, reduce loud noises, and schedule a vet visit to rule out medical causes.

title: The Fascinating World of Cats: Why We Love Our Furry Friends
author: Thompson P.
summary: From ancient temples to modern apartments, cats keep winning human hearts with independence and charm.
content: History shows cats moving from grain protectors to household royalty. Their mix of self-reliance and selective affection makes each bond feel earned.
Daily enrichment matters: rotate toys, use puzzle feeders, and add window perches so indoor cats can safely watch the world.
Healthy cats need routine: fresh water, measured meals, and vet checkups twice a year. Small habits prevent costly emergencies later.

title: Finding Motivation: Tiny Habits for Consistent Creativity
author: Apitarn P.
summary: Creative ruts rarely need grand plans. Use short timed sprints, frictionless setups, and generous drafts to keep moving.
content: Start with 10-minute blocks. A visible timer reduces decision fatigue and proves that small wins accumulate.
Lower the bar for a first draft—aim for a 'bad first pass' that you can refine. Momentum matters more than perfection on day one.
End sessions with a short note about what to do next. Future-you will thank present-you for a clear starting point.

title: The Science of the Cat's Purr: More Than a Happy Sound
author: Thompson P.
summary: Purring sits between communication and healing. Frequencies between 25–150 Hz may aid tissue repair for cats—and maybe humans.
content: Cats purr when relaxed, but also when hurt. The vibration may be self-soothing or even supportive for bone density and wound recovery.
Notice context: a relaxed posture plus kneading suggests contentment, while purring with dilated pupils or flattened ears can signal pain.
If your cat purrs while hiding or refusing food, schedule a vet check. Pain behaviors can be subtle.

title: Unlocking Creativity with Constraints
author: Apitarn P.
summary: Limit choices to open new ideas. Short deadlines, smaller palettes, and word counts reduce overthinking and spark momentum.
content: Pick a single theme for a week and ship daily variations. Repetition reveals patterns you can reuse or remix later.
Use constraints to warm up: write with only 100 words or sketch with two colors. The restriction frees you to focus on structure.
Review constraints often. If one stops helping, replace it instead of dropping practice altogether.

title: Top 10 Health Tips Every Cat Owner Should Know
author: Thompson P.
summary: Keep cats thriving with simple routines: fresh water, measured meals, and litter box hygiene prevent most avoidable vet visits.
content: Hydration is the easiest health upgrade. Offer multiple water bowls or a fountain, especially for cats on dry food.
Keep the litter box rule: one per cat plus one extra. Scoop daily to avoid accidents and urinary issues.
Schedule preventive care twice a year. Early dental cleanings and vaccines cost far less than emergency treatments.
